skill.name: browser-automation

skill.summary: Build reliable browser automation with Playwright, Puppeteer, strong selectors, test isolation, and trace-based debugging.

security_audit.summary: The static shell execution finding is a false positive caused by Markdown inline code on the related skills line. The skill has no executable files, but its prose includes dual-use anti-detection and stealth guidance for scraping.

remediation.suggestion: Limit stealth plugin and delay guidance to authorized testing. Add clear compliance boundaries for scraping and browser automation.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 70 uses Markdown inline backticks to list related skill names, not Ruby or shell execution. There is no executable code or command interpolation at this location.

semantic_findings.title: Dual-Use Anti-Detection Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill references anti-detection patterns, stealth plugins, and delays between requests. This can help authorized testing, but it can also support bypassing website anti-bot controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly mentions anti-detection patterns and stealth plugins. The risk is dual-use because the context is browser scraping, not credential theft or malware.

content.value_statement: Browser scripts often fail because selectors, waits, and browser state are fragile. This skill guides reliable Playwright and Puppeteer automation for tests, scraping, and agent workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose Playwright, Puppeteer, or Selenium alternatives.
Recommends user-facing locators instead of brittle CSS or XPath selectors.
Covers Playwright auto-wait patterns for stable browser interactions.
Describes isolated browser contexts for independent test runs.
Highlights trace capture, viewport consistency, and popup wait issues.
Identifies scraping reliability concerns such as delays and detection systems.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or installed automation dependencies.
Does not provide a complete framework template or test runner setup.
Scraping guidance must follow website terms and applicable law.
Anti-detection guidance is dual-use and should stay within authorized work.

use_cases.title: Stabilize End-to-End Tests
use_cases.description: Improve flaky Playwright or Puppeteer tests by using better locators, waits, and isolated browser state.

use_cases.title: Plan Responsible Web Scraping
use_cases.description: Review scraping workflows for reliability, rate limits, monitoring, and compliance boundaries before implementation.

use_cases.title: Guide Browser-Based Agents
use_cases.description: Design agent browser actions that use visible page behavior, predictable waits, and recoverable workflow steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Browser Framework
prompt_templates.prompt: I need browser automation for [testing or scraping]. Compare Playwright and Puppeteer for my use case, constraints, and team skills.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Flaky Browser Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this failing browser test behavior: [describe failure]. Identify likely selector, wait, state, and viewport problems.

prompt_templates.title: Design Isolated Test Runs
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Playwright test structure for [application]. Include browser context isolation, trace capture, locator strategy, and popup handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Automation Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this browser automation plan for reliability and compliance risk: [describe plan]. Flag detection, rate limit, consent, and monitoring concerns.

output_examples.input: A QA engineer asks why a login test fails only in continuous integration.
output: The response checks viewport differences, missing auto-waits, shared browser state, and selectors that depend on layout.
It recommends user-facing locators, fresh contexts, and trace capture for failed runs.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether to use Puppeteer or Playwright for a new automation project.
output: The response compares browser support, locator reliability, waiting behavior, ecosystem needs, and Chrome-only constraints.
It recommends Playwright unless the project depends on Puppeteer-specific stealth tooling.

output_examples.input: A data team asks for a scraping workflow review before launch.
output: The response reviews rate limits, monitoring, retries, content stability, and authorization boundaries.
It warns that anti-detection techniques should only support approved testing or compliant data access.

best_practices: Prefer user-facing locators that match what users can see.
Let Playwright auto-wait for readiness instead of adding fixed sleeps.
Run each test with isolated browser state and collect traces for failures.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on CSS or XPath selectors before accessible locators.
Do not share one browser context across unrelated tests.
Do not use stealth or delay tactics to bypass access controls.

faq.question: Does this skill install Playwright or Puppeteer?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance only and does not install packages or run commands.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is Playwright always better than Puppeteer?
faq.answer: No. The skill favors Playwright for most cases, but Puppeteer can fit Chrome-only projects.

faq.question: Does it cover web scraping?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers scraping reliability, but users must follow site terms and applicable law.

faq.question: Does it include test design patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers test isolation, user-facing locators, and Playwright auto-wait behavior.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The main concern is dual-use anti-detection guidance that could be misused outside authorized work.
